title: Trump Demands Investigation into Commerce Department, Alleging Pre-Election GDP Numbers Were 'Fake'
snippet: Following a routine upward revision of third-quarter economic growth to 4.3%, President Donald Trump accused federal statisticians of deliberately underreporting data prior to the midterm elections.
content:
WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. — President Donald Trump lashed out at his own administration on Thursday, accusing the Commerce Department of intentionally withholding stronger economic growth data prior to the midterm elections and demanding a formal investigation into federal statisticians.

The president's sharp critique followed a standard update released Wednesday by the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA), which revised third-quarter Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth upward to an annualized rate of 4.3%, up from an initial estimate of 3.4%.

Allegations of Pre-Election Misconduct

Posting on social media over the Thanksgiving holiday, Trump framed the earlier data as a political hit job aimed at hurting Republicans, who lost control of both houses of Congress in the Nov. 3 midterms.

"It was just revealed that the REAL Numbers on the Economy, published before the Election, were FAKE, and a correction was issued yesterday by the people in the Government Agency that does these numbers," Trump wrote, calling the adjustment a "massive, and purposeful, error" and requesting an "immediate investigation."

Government data agencies routinely update economic statistics like GDP and monthly employment reports as more comprehensive data sets become available. These scheduled revisions occur independently of political events. The Commerce Department did not immediately respond to requests for comment due to the federal holiday.

Pattern of Discrediting Economic Indicators

This latest clash highlights Trump's ongoing strategy of questioning official statistics whenever they conflict with his preferred economic narrative. In August 2025, Trump ousted the commissioner of the Bureau of Labor Statistics after a weak jobs report showed only 73,000 jobs added in July and downgraded prior months by 258,000 jobs—figures he labeled as "rigged."

Market analysts warn that undermining public trust in official government benchmarks creates volatility for businesses, financial markets, and investors who rely on impartial data to make strategic decisions.

Voter Disconnect and Inflation Concerns

While Trump frequently highlights positive growth metrics, voters have shown skepticism about the health of the economy. AP Voter Poll data from the midterm elections revealed that 76% of voters viewed economic conditions as "not so good" or "poor," with nearly two-thirds asserting that the administration's fiscal policies have exacerbated inflation.

In his holiday posts, Trump conspicuously omitted another key metric released alongside the revised GDP data on Wednesday: the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge, which accelerated to a 3.8% annualized rate in October.
